neighbours.label: ' through' after a verb of motion or cutting (passing through a space or medium)
fire: After lunch the two hikers wandered slowly through the pine forest near the lake.
A cold draft was blowing through the gaps in the old cabin walls all night.
The little boat drifted through the narrow canal under a dozen stone bridges.
Every morning she jogs through the park before heading to the office.
The new highway will slice through the farmland east of the town.
We drove for hours through the desert without seeing another car.
The deer bolted through the tall grass as soon as it heard us.
Sunlight streamed through the dusty window of the empty classroom.

notes: card: ' through' x15 of top 32 (walked through, cut through, chase down the road through the trees); ' wind' also fires. Near misses swap in another preposition and avoid wind.
